title: The Ehrhart–Zeta duality conjecture for linear arbors
statement:
Let $t$ be a **linear arbor**, meaning an arbor in which each vertex has at most one sub-tree. Let $\operatorname{Rev}(t)$ be its reverse, obtained by putting the vertices in the opposite order. Let $Q_t$ be the associated polytope, $E_t(u)$ its Ehrhart polynomial, and $P_t$ its associated poset with Zeta polynomial $Z_t(u)$.

**The Ehrhart–Zeta duality conjecture.** For every linear arbor $t$,

$$
E_t(u)=Z_{\operatorname{Rev}(t)}(u+1).
$$

The conjecture would identify the normalized volume of $Q_t$ with the number of maximal chains of $P_{\operatorname{Rev}(t)}$. The source presents this as open and notes a further expected h-vector symmetry under reversal.
source_name: Frédéric Chapoton, “On posets and polytopes attached to arbors”, arXiv:2503.04247 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.04247

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).
